messages:
alex: Heads-up — we got a pulse alert this morning: a single org is using a bursty pattern and it's chewing through shared-pool capacity. Seeing tail latency spikes for a few other tenants.
ops-bot: [alert] high_p99_latency in pool gpu-v2-west (since 06:12 UTC). top offender api_key=org_42_key (rate profile: 2.3k req/min sustained bursts).
tara: Ugh. Is this noisy neighbor or a legit traffic spike? Any customer SLA impact so far?
sanjay: Looks noisy to me — traffic is very bursty, short-lived but huge peaks. Their average QPS is normal outside bursts. p95 stays ok but p99 jumps.
emily: We should be careful not to throttle legitimate flash-sale customers. We need per-org smoothing + graceful degradation before hard reject.
ben: Agreed. Proposal: implement a two-tier enforcement model: per-key token-bucket for hard caps + per-org smoothing layer that shapes bursts to the customer's reserved/burst budget.
alex: Sketch of how that could look in runtime config:

```
service_enforcement:
  per_key: { cap_qps: 500, penalty: 429 }
  per_org_smoothing:
    window: 60s
    max_burst_tokens: 2000
    refill_rate: 33/s
    ejection_policy: "probabilistic_degrade"
```

alex: Smoothing would sit in the front router and rewrite request_rate to backend when burst > budget. Then runtime will try to batch and cache more aggressively for shaped traffic.
tara: For rollout UX, console needs to show: current burst budget, refill rate, recent ejections, and a preview of how shaping affects p99/throughput. Ops needs an override to clamp a tenant quickly.
emily: Also want to expose simulated-impact button: "Preview shaping for org X" that runs a short dry-run and shows expected latency/cost changes.
sanjay: Detection side: add a telemetry rule that tags a tenant as "burst-prone" when bursts > 3x baseline for 3 windows in 24h. That feed should drive auto-smoothing suggestions in Optimize.
ben: How does this interact with Dedicated customers? They might have reserved capacity and should be exempt from smoothing unless we detect abuse.
alex: Right — we need policy precedence: Dedicated/reserved -> tenant-specific overrides -> global smoothing. Console should show precedence chain.
ops-bot: [note] created issue #INF-2312: "per-org smoothing prototype + console preview" (assign: sanjay, priority: P2).
emily: One implementation detail — if we shape and delay tokens, we should still surface a clear error code to clients so SDKs can surface guidance. Maybe `429` for hard rejects, `202` or `429x` for shaped requests? Need compatibility discussion.
tara: I'd push for returning 202 with header `X-Redwood-Shaped: true` when we accept but queue/shape. That keeps user requests progressing vs failing.
sanjay: Hmm 202 might be confusing for sync generation endpoints. We could do `200` with a header and slightly slower tail, but clients expecting low-latency might misinterpret. Another option: streaming partial tokens while shaping.
ben: From billing side, shaped requests should still bill but with a note (reduced unit price?) — otherwise customers will escalate if we purposely slow them but still charge full.
emily: We should coordinate with finance. Suggest: bill at normal rate up to reserved, then discounted rate for shaped/queued tokens (since we save backend cost via batching).
alex: For telemetry dashboards: add a per-org "smoothing score" (0-100) and time-series of shaped qps vs raw qps. Need to expose the top bursting keys, recent ejection events, and downstream impact on p99.
tara: UX: when we show a suggested smoothing policy in console, include an "apply as canary" option that runs for 10 minutes against 5% of traffic and posts a canary report.
ops-bot: [deploy-bot] rolled out routing patch v0.31 to staging with smoothing hooks enabled.
ben: Let's be explicit about emergency ejection: if a tenant's burst causes >10% p99 regression cluster-wide for >2m, auto-eject to a lower tier (probabilistic drop) and create a high-priority incident.
especially_sanjay: (lol) that username is wrong — ignore
sanjay: ha, ignore that. Back to policy, we also need a feedback loop so Optimize can recommend quantization or batch size changes for the noisy tenant's model variant.
emily: TL;DR action items: 1) prototype front-router smoothing (sanjay), 2) console preview UI (tara + emily), 3) billing policy draft (ben), 4) telemetry rules & smoothing score (alex). I'll book async design review.
alex: Thanks — can someone put a short runbook for ops emergency ejection? We should document the manual override steps.
tara: I'll add a step-by-step in the new INF-2312 ticket and attach mockups. :thumbsup:
ben: I'll sync with finance tomorrow.
alex: Cool. If we don't hear objections, I'll queue a small canary in the next deploy window.
emily: No objections from me. :+1:
ops-bot: [note] INF-2312 updated: added runbook draft and initial telemetry queries.
